Looks as though we won't see each other for a while, Pete."  "What ship are you getting?"  "The _Lord Nelson_."  It was Wayne's turn to laugh. "It looks as though we _will_ be seeing each other.

arxiv-2103-10876.title: Fluctuation control of non-thermal orbital order
arxiv-2103-10876.creator: Francesco Grandi, Martin Eckstein
arxiv-2103-10876.description: Abstract Orbitally ordered states exhibit unique features which make them a promising platform for exploring the ultrafast dynamics of long-range order in solids: Their free energy typically has multiple discrete minima, and electric laser fields or selectively excited phonons can exert effective forces that may be used to steer the order parameter through these free energy landscapes.

arxiv-2108-07570.title: Quantum optics meets black hole thermodynamics via conformal quantum mechanics: I. Master equation for acceleration radiation
arxiv-2108-07570.creator: A. Azizi, H. E. Camblong, A. Chakraborty, C. R. Ordóñez, M. O. Scully
arxiv-2108-07570.description: Abstract A quantum-optics approach is used to study the nature of the acceleration radiation due to a random atomic cloud falling freely into a generalized Schwarzschild black hole through a Boulware vacuum. The properties of this horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) are analyzed with a master equation that is fully developed in a multimode format.

arxiv-2111-00300.title: Introducing Fermionic Link Models
arxiv-2111-00300.creator: Lukas Rammelmüller
arxiv-2111-00300.description: Abstract Quantum link models (QLMs) are extensions of Wilson-type lattice gauge theories, and show rich physics beyond the phenomena of conventional Wilson gauge theories. Here we explore the physics of U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) symmetric QLMs, both using a more conventional quantum spin-1/2 representation, as well as a fermionic representation.

arxiv-2203-13401.title: Tensor Perturbations and Thick Branes in Higher Dimensional Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
arxiv-2203-13401.creator: Yongqun Xu, Xiangdong Zhang
arxiv-2203-13401.description: Abstract A thick brane model with Gauss-Bonnet action in a homogeneous anisotropic D = ( 4 + 1 + d ) D=(4+1+d) spacetime is studied. By choosing a concrete metric ansatz, we show that this spacetime is stable against linear tensor perturbations under certain conditions. The graviton zero modes are also given.

arxiv-2205-08829.title: Random motions in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} with orthogonal directions
arxiv-2205-08829.creator: Fabrizio Cinque, Enzo Orsingher Department of Statistical Sciences, Sapienza University of Rome, Italy
arxiv-2205-08829.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Fabrizio Cinque, Enzo Orsingher Department of Statistical Sciences, Sapienza University of Rome, Italy. This paper is devoted to the detailed analysis of three-dimensional motions in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} with orthogonal directions switching at Poisson times and moving with constant speed c > 0 c>0 .

arxiv-2208-00886.title: Efficient in-situ generation of photon-memory entanglement in a nonlinear cavity
arxiv-2208-00886.creator: Hoi-Kwan Lau, Hong Qiao, Aashish A. Clerk, Tian Zhong
arxiv-2208-00886.description: Abstract Combining parametric driving and photon-atomic memory coupling within one optical cavity, we describe a scheme for in-situ generation of multimode photon-memory entanglement. We find that precise cavity impedance matching is neither required nor optimal to achieve high-rate entanglement for quantum networks.

arxiv-2308-12930.title: Explicit generators for the relation module in the example of Gruenberg–Linnell
arxiv-2308-12930.creator: W. H. Mannan School of Computing, Engineering and Mathematics, University of Brighton, Cockroft Building, Lewes Road, Brighton BN2 4GJ email: wajid@mannan.info
arxiv-2308-12930.description: Abstract Gruenberg and Linnell showed that the standard relation module of a free product of n n groups of the form C r × ℤ C_{r}\times\mathbb{Z} could be generated by just n + 1 n+1 generators, raising the possibility of a relation gap. We explicitly give such a set of generators.

arxiv-2405-02641.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Artur E. Semushin \auno 1,2, Evgeny Yu. Soldatov \auno 1. Parameterization of heavy effects beyond the Standard Model is available using higher-dimension operators of the effective field theory and their Wilson coefficients, where their values are not known. Experimental sensitivity to the Wilson coefficients can be significantly changed in case of the usage of composite anomalous signal, which contains anomalous contributions from background processes in addition to the conventional ones from the signal process.

arxiv-2406-11624.title: Words in Motion: Extracting Interpretable Control Vectors for Motion Transformers
arxiv-2406-11624.creator: Ömer Şahin Taş, Royden Wagner *
arxiv-2406-11624.description: Abstract Transformer-based models generate hidden states that are difficult to interpret. In this work, we analyze hidden states and modify them at inference, with a focus on motion forecasting. We use linear probing to analyze whether interpretable features are embedded in hidden states. Our experiments reveal high probing accuracy, indicating latent space regularities with functionally important directions.

arxiv-2506-06485.title: What Is Seen Cannot Be Unseen: The Disruptive Effect of Knowledge Conflict on Large Language Models
arxiv-2506-06485.creator: Kaiser Sun, Fan Bai, Mark Dredze, fbai3@jh.edu, mdredze@cs.jhu.edu
arxiv-2506-06485.description: Abstract Large language models frequently rely on both contextual input and parametric knowledge to perform tasks. However, these sources can come into conflict, especially when retrieved documents contradict the model’s parametric knowledge. We propose a diagnostic framework to systematically evaluate LLM behavior under context-memory conflict , where the contextual information diverges from their parametric beliefs.

arxiv-2506-22977.title: On the Generalizability of "Competition of Mechanisms: Tracing How Language Models Handle Facts and Counterfactuals"
arxiv-2506-22977.creator: Asen Dotsinski asen.dotsinski@student.uva.nl, Udit Thakur udit.thakur@student.uva.nl, Marko Ivanov marko.ivanov@student.uva.nl, Mohammad Hafeez Khan hafeez.khan@student.uva.nl, Maria Heuss m.c.heuss@uva.nl
arxiv-2506-22977.description: Abstract We present a reproduction study of "Competition of Mechanisms: Tracing How Language Models Handle Facts and Counterfactuals" ( Ortu et al. 2024 ) , which investigates competition of mechanisms in language models between factual recall and counterfactual in-context repetition.

arxiv-2507-09049.title: CMER: A Context-Aware Approach for Mining Ethical Concern-related App Reviews
arxiv-2507-09049.creator: Aakash Sorathiya, Gouri Ginde
arxiv-2507-09049.description: Abstract With the increasing proliferation of mobile applications in our daily lives, the concerns surrounding ethics have surged significantly. Users communicate their feedback in app reviews, frequently emphasizing ethical concerns, such as privacy and security. Incorporating these reviews has proved to be useful for many areas of software engineering (e.g., requirement engineering, testing, etc.).

pmc-10693143.title: Women’s autonomy in healthcare decision making: a systematic review
pmc-10693143.creator: Idayu Badilla Idris, Amy Azira Hamis, Ayuzeity Bistari Md Bukhori, David Chan Chee Hoong, Hakimah Yusop, Muhammad Al-Amin Shaharuddin, Nazmeen Adline Fawwazah A. Fauzi, Thinakaran Kandayah
pmc-10693143.description: ObjectivesAlthough there are calls for women’s empowerment and gender equity globally, there are still large disparities regarding women’s autonomy in healthcare decision making. The autonomy of women is believed to be crucial in improving their health-related outcomes. This review discusses factors that influence autonomy among women in healthcare decision making.DesignSystematic review.

pmc-10710534.title: Managing a Pseudo-Mobitz Type II Atrioventricular (AV) Block Intrapartum: A Case Report
pmc-10710534.creator: Mohd Khairi Othman, Muhammad Zulkifli Konok, Engku Husna Engku Ismail, Zurkurnai Yusof, W Yus Haniff W Isa
pmc-10710534.description: Atrioventricular (AV) block in pregnancy is rare, but it is a serious arrhythmia that needs to be carefully managed in pregnancy. However, as of now, there are no clear guidelines or consensus for intrapartum management. Most of the time, an intrapartum AV block is secondary to hypervagatonic sinus node dysfunction and is treated conservatively.

pmc-11359194.title: YOLOv5s-BiPCNeXt, a Lightweight Model for Detecting Disease in Eggplant Leaves
pmc-11359194.creator: Zhedong Xie, Chao Li, Zhuang Yang, Zhen Zhang, Jiazhuo Jiang, Hongyu Guo
pmc-11359194.description: Ensuring the healthy growth of eggplants requires the precise detection of leaf diseases, which can significantly boost yield and economic income. Improving the efficiency of plant disease identification in natural scenes is currently a crucial issue. This study aims to provide an efficient detection method suitable for disease detection in natural scenes. A lightweight detection model, YOLOv5s-BiPCNeXt, is proposed.

However, ceftazidime-avibactam-resistant (CAZ/AVI-R) Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae) has emerged during treatment for CRKP infection. pmc-12564498.title: Benzo[d]imidazole–Naphthalen-Arylmethanone Regioisomers as CB1 Ligands: Evaluation of Agonism via an Indirect Cytotoxicity-Based Approach
pmc-12564498.creator: Analia Young Hwa Cho, Renato Burgos Ravanal, Valeria Zuñiga Salazar, Marco Mellado, Marcos Lorca, David Pessoa-Mahana, Jaime Mella, Germán Günther Sapunar, Javier Romero-Parra, Grace Blest Hopley
pmc-12564498.description: CB1 agonist compounds may be potential drug candidates for the treatment of gliomas, as they have been shown to inhibit tumor cell proliferation, induce apoptosis, and reduce angiogenesis in various preclinical models. Their ability to modulate the endocannabinoid system suggests a promising therapeutic approach for targeting glioma growth and progression.

pmc-12628543.title: Risk factors for catastrophic healthcare expenditure and high economic burden for children with anorectal malformations in Southwestern Uganda
pmc-12628543.creator: Felix Oyania, Caroline Q. Stephens, Sarah Ullrich, Amy M. Shui, Meera Kotagal, Godfrey Zari Rukundo, Joseph Ngonzi, Ava Yap, Francis Bajunirwe, Dan Poenaru, Doruk E. Ozgediz
pmc-12628543.description: BackgroundAnorectal malformations (ARMs) are common congenital anomalies in low-and middle-income countries (LMICs), and they are often repaired in a staged manner. High out-of-pocket (OOP) payment for surgical care in many LMICs makes households vulnerable to catastrophic health expenditures (CHE). ARM patients often require multiple operations and hospitalizations, which may make them vulnerable to CHE.

pmc-13006971.title: Drug screening for α-synuclein aggregation inhibitors via multimodal graph neural network
pmc-13006971.creator: Tingle Gu, Zixu Ran, Wenyin Li, Xudong Guo, Bo Li, Fuyi Li, Cangzhi Jia
pmc-13006971.description: The pathological aggregation of α-synuclein (α-syn) constitutes a pivotal hallmark in the progression of neurodegenerative disorders, including Parkinson’s disease, underscoring the imperative need for identifying site-specific ligands. This study presents, for the first time, an advanced deep learning framework specifically designed for the prediction of molecular properties associated with α-syn.

pmc-13185623.title: Assessment of hPod measured by fNIRS as an indicator of brain development in preterm infants
pmc-13185623.creator: Anna Shiraki, Hama Watanabe, Takafumi Ushida, Ayano Yanagisawa, Misa Hashimoto, Misae Yamada, Hajime Narita, Takamasa Mitsumatsu, Ryosuke Suzui, Masahiro Kawaguchi, Yuji Ito, Hiroyuki Yamamoto, Tomohiko Nakata, Yoshiaki Sato, Jun Natsume, Gentaro Taga, Hiroyuki Kidokoro
pmc-13185623.description: The brain undergoes dramatic development during early life, particularly throughout the third trimester of pregnancy. Preterm infants experience this critical period in the extrauterine environment, which may alter brain development and has recently gained attention for its potential impact on subsequent neurodevelopmental challenges. Brain maturation involves not only neuronal growth but also the development of vascular and neurovascular coupling systems.

pmc-13267644.title: On the dynamic caddisfly silk H-fibroin gene: a population study in a net-spinning species
pmc-13267644.creator: Russell J Stewart, Ashlyn Powell, Jacqueline Heckenhauer, Steffen U Pauls, Gabriela Jijon, Samantha Standring, Cheryl Y Hayashi, Richard H Baker, Paul B Frandsen, Amanda Larracuente
pmc-13267644.description: Larvae of the caddisfly Arctopsyche grandis BANKS build protective structures and spin silken capture nets in flowing water. Caddisfly H-fibroin, the major protein component of its silk fibers, has a blocky structure with repeating units defined as beginning with a [(SX)nE]m region followed by a G-rich spacer.

pmc-13350313.title: Geopolitics, international collaborations and publication ethics
pmc-13350313.creator: Olle ten Cate, Vanessa C Burch, Stanley J Hamstra, Lindsey M Pope, Jennifer Weller
pmc-13350313.description: Short abstractGeopolitics, international collaborations, and publication ethic ‐‐ how does it affect HPE scholarship? #MedEd The interference of politics in science is a growing concern in universities and health care institutions. 1 , 2 More than in the past, universities face tensions with governments interfering in areas of research that do not support governmental policies.

pmc-13404609.title: Helicobacter pylori Eradication in the Era of Antibiotic Resistance: From Universal Regimens to Precision-Guided Management
pmc-13404609.creator: Ayman Elbehiry, Eman Marzouk
pmc-13404609.description: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection represents a major global health challenge and a leading cause of peptic ulcer disease and gastric cancer. The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance has progressively reduced the effectiveness of traditional empirical eradication regimens, highlighting the need for more individualized treatment approaches. This review evaluates the evolving transition from empirical therapy toward precision-guided H.

pmc-13457951.title: Ammonium sulfate provides an efficient method for isolating small extracellular vesicles from human biofluids
pmc-13457951.creator: Qimeng Li, Zinan Guo, Yu Li, Menglu Zhang, Yunxia Yao, Xuemin Wang, Lifang Zhao, Yanning Cai
pmc-13457951.description: Small extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanosized vesicles (< 200 nm) secreted from various tissues, including the central nervous system (CNS), into diverse biofluids. Due to their ability to carry molecular cargo that reflects the physiological state of their parental cells, small EVs represent promising diagnostic carriers for neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease (PD).
